result.title: State Representation Shapes Long-Horizon Agent Learning and Transfer: An Empirical Study
result.summary: An end-to-end success rate alone cannot distinguish failure to learn an action from failure to apply it as task state changes. We study this distinction in deterministic tool workflows that provide the current artifact state and candidate action recipes. Using 1.7B, 8B, and 27B Qwen models, we compare supervised learning across workflow horizons and cross the state representation used for training with the one used at evaluation. Horizon-matched supervision yields high completion, but an H4-trained 1.7B model transfers poorly to longer workflows under full-state observations. In an H16 crossover, compact-trained 1.7B adapters complete 50/50 held-out tasks in compact view and 0/50 in full view for each of three paired training seeds; full-trained outcomes vary across seeds. A separate 8B adapter pair shows a similar asymmetry. The view dependence also appears in paired-choice tasks where both candidate calls are executable and the correct choice depends on table contents; here, the compact mask does not consult the target action. An explicit relevance cue improves full-view execution but does not close the gap for the tested checkpoint. In a separate 27B ScienceWorld study, compact-state training improves local accuracy under both views, indicating that the transfer pattern depends on the task and observation construction. Together, these experiments identify representation-sensitive transfer as a bottleneck in the controlled workflows, without isolating content reduction from other changes to the observation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在提供当前工件状态与候选动作的确定性工具工作流中，用 Qwen 1.7B/8B/27B 比较不同工作流长度下的监督学习，并交叉训练期与评估期使用的状态表示，考察长程 agent 的学习与迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「紧凑 vs 完整状态」的交叉表示协议，以及「紧凑掩码不查阅目标动作」所暗示的信息坍缩与表示敏感迁移，可能为 LVR 中内部状态保留哪些任务必要信息、视觉旁路与长度泛化提供可核查线索。
